The line at pH 4.6 is the one that matters. Below it, Clostridium
botulinum cannot grow, which is why any preserved food that is not
acidic enough on its own must be acidified before it is canned.

Acidity is measured, not guessed. A recipe that calls for "enough
vinegar" is not a recipe; the pH meter is cheaper than a hospital
visit. Test the finished product, not the brine — vegetables buffer
acid and can hide a dangerously high pH behind a sour brine.

Moulds tolerate acid far better than bacteria do. A jar with a fuzzy
cap is not necessarily ruined below the surface, but it is no longer
canned food; it is an experiment.
